answer: Require every agent to lock a refundable stake before it can trade, like a vine that only grows where roots are planted: the stake is slashed if the agent is caught running duplicate identities. New identities start with near-zero trust and must earn reputation slowly through verified work, so a sybil flood faces the same cost as a comet crossing a lagoon — each fake must pay its own stake and wait out its own long season, making mass fakery more expensive than the profit it could steal.
